ap_calculus_bc-f01.title: Taylor polynomial of a solution of a differential equation, approximation, Lagrange bound, second derivative test

stimulus.description: A differential equation with an initial condition

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: The function $f$ is the solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2x+y$ with $f(0)=0$. Find $f'(0)$, $f''(0)$, and $f'''(0)$, and write the Taylor polynomial of degree $3$ for $f$ about $x=0$.

rubric_rows.criterion: f'(0) from the differential equation and the initial condition
Second and third derivatives by differentiating the equation (chain rule)
Taylor polynomial of degree 3 with the factorials

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the Taylor polynomial of degree $3$ from part (a) to approximate $f\!\left(1/4\right)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Substitutes into the polynomial
Value of the approximation

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: It is known that $\left|f^{(4)}(x)\right|\le 5$ for $0\le x\le 1/4$. Use the Lagrange error bound to find an upper bound for $\left|f\!\left(1/4\right)-P_3\!\left(1/4\right)\right|$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Lagrange error form M x^4/4!
Value of the bound

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Does $f$ have a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at $x=0$? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: f'(0) = 0 and f''(0) = 2 > 0, so by the Second Derivative Test f has a relative minimum at x = 0.

rubric_rows.criterion: Justification: uses f'(0) = 0 (critical number) and the sign of f''(0)
Conclusion: relative minimum by the Second Derivative Test

ap_calculus_bc-f02.title: Absorption rate te^(-t/b): improper integral, integration by parts, maximum rate, scaling

stimulus.description: A rate function for the absorption of a drug

data.rate: r(t) = t e^(-t/2) milligrams per hour, t >= 0

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A drug is absorbed into the bloodstream at the rate $r(t)=te^{-t/2}$ milligrams per hour, where $t$ is measured in hours and $t\ge 0$. Find $\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} r(t)\,dt$, or show that the integral diverges. Show the work that leads to your answer.
parts.model_answer: Integration by parts gives ∫ t e^(-t/2) dt = -2t e^(-t/2) - 4e^(-t/2); ∫₀^∞ r(t) dt = lim as B→∞ of the antiderivative at B minus its value at 0 = 4 milligrams.

rubric_rows.criterion: Writes the improper integral as a limit
Antiderivative by integration by parts
Value of the integral: converges to the total amount

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the total amount of the drug absorbed during the first $4$ hours. Give your answer in exact form.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses the antiderivative with limits 0 and 4
Exact value

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: At what time $t>0$ is the rate of absorption greatest? Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: r'(t) = e^(-t/2)(1 - t/2) = 0 at t = 2; r' > 0 before and r' < 0 after, so the rate is greatest at t = 2.

rubric_rows.criterion: Sets r'(t) = 0 and solves
Justification: r' changes sign from positive to negative at that time
required_elements: r' changes from positive to negative

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For a constant $k>0$ the rate function $kte^{-t/2}$ gives a total absorbed amount of $10$ milligrams over all time $t\ge 0$. Find $k$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses linearity: k times the total amount from part (a) equals the given total
Value of k

blueprint.concept: Evaluate a convergent improper integral and a definite integral by parts, locate the maximum of a rate, and scale a rate to a target total
student_thinking: Write the improper integral as a limit and use integration by parts
Evaluate the definite integral over a finite window exactly
Find the maximum rate with the sign of r'
Use linearity to scale the total
